channel.description: Latest articles from The Garden Island (thegardenisland.com)

item.title: Happy Camper for Friday, February 6, 2026
item.description: We used to have a pikake (the Western term is jasmine) garden at Kilohana, said Gina Medrano, an associate with Malie Organics, a boutique that offers a variety of hair, body and skin care and beauty products that are based on hydrosols utilizing locally grown (not just Kauai) fruits and flowers.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Scrutinize pause of tax cuts for all
item.description: Good intentions went into Act 46, the 2024 tax reform legislation that implemented the largest income tax cut in state history. Hawaii is one of the nation’s notoriously highest-tax states, and the state’s tax structure was due for a revamp.

item.title: Okinawan Lifeguard Exchange Program certificate ceremony set
item.description: LIHUE — The Kauai Ocean Safety Bureau, in partnership with the Okinawan Lifesaving Association and the Hawaiian Lifeguard Association, will host a certificate ceremony on Feb. 20, at 10 a.m. at the Moikeha Rotunda in Lihue.

item.title: Hawaii’s jobless rate tied for lowest in U.S.
item.description: Hawaii now shares the distinction of having the lowest unemployment rate in the country.

item.title: Work begins on centralized kitchen on Oahu to modernize school meals
item.description: A new regional centralized kitchen facility in Whitmore Village aims to modernize public school meal preparation, expand the use of locally sourced ingredients and improve efficiency across Hawaii’s school cafeterias.

item.title: Caution urged for mariners during peak humpback whale season
item.description: HONOLULU — More than 10,000 humpback whales migrate to Hawaii each winter to breed, nurse calves and raise their young. As kohola, or humpback whale, season reaches its peak in Hawaii, the Go Slow – Whales Below initiative urges mariners to be mindful and exercise caution when out on the ocean, for the safety of the whales and everyone on the water.

item.title: World War II nisei soldiers from Hawaii receive posthumous promotions
item.description: Seven soldiers from the islands who were expelled from University of Hawaii’s Reserve Officer Training Corps for their Japanese heritage and went on to die fighting the Nazis in Europe as enlisted men were posthumously promoted Monday to the rank of 2nd lieutenant.

item.title: Kauai sees the most whales statewide according to most recent count
item.description: According to the statewide results of the Sanctuary Ocean Count released on Thursday, Kauai saw more whales during the count period than any of the other participating islands.

item.title: Chickenpox outbreak doubles, expands to more schools
item.description: The Hawaii Department of Health reports the community outbreak of chickenpox on Kauai has expanded, raising concerns the highly contagious disease will continue to spread.

item.title: High Surf Warning in effect through Saturday
item.description: LIHUE — The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Warning for north- and west-facing shores of Kauai and Niihau currently in effect through 6 p.m. Saturday. The warning may be extended, dropped or modified as conditions develop.
